_note: Renamed from sailor_patient_twospecies_fit_search_space.json on 2026-10-02. Search space of scripts/patient_cmaes_fit.py with --solver twospecies: the CMA-ES fit of TwoCompartmentWithNutrientFKPPSolver (proliferative P, necrotic N, nutrient) to one SAILOR patient, written 2026-10-01. The format is that of patient_fit_search_space.json (the isotropic fit's file): keys starting with '_' are comments; an entry {"min", "max", "scale"} is a fitted factor; any other entry is a fixed value, written into every run config when it is a solver parameter or consumed by the script's derivations when it is not; "solver" is checked; the order of the factor entries is the coordinate order of the unit cube. The ten factors of the isotropic fit (front_speed_mm_per_day, front_width_mm, seed_sigma_mm, seed_peak_density, growth_length_mm, seed_bbox_x/y/z, rt_alpha, chemo_kill_rate) and the four fixed values keep that file's ranges, scales, derivations and reasons (its _growth_band, _clock, _seed, _seed_band, _seed_position, _chemo, _chemo_decay_rate, _radiotherapy, _fixed, _units, _sources), with the caveat of _growth_band below; the four two-compartment parameters necrosis_rate, nutrient_threshold, nutrient_diffusivity and nutrient_consumption_rate are fitted as well (_twospecies). Everything not listed comes from the base config (fisher_kpp_jax/configs/TwoCompartmentWithNutrientFKPPSolver_stupp.json by default).
_invariance: The (v, lambda, l) coordinates are chosen for the rescaling invariance explained in _invariance of patient_fit_search_space.json; in the two-compartment model the rescaling D, rho -> s D, s rho, t -> t / s leaves the pre-op fit flat only if necrosis_rate, nutrient_diffusivity and nutrient_consumption_rate are rescaled by s as well, so the unidentified direction is no longer a single axis but the ray along v and those three rates (all four log-uniform, so a straight line in the unit cube).
_growth_band: D = v lambda / 2 and rho = v / (2 lambda) from the front speed v and width lambda, as in the isotropic fit. In the two-compartment model the growth term is rho * nutrient * P (1 - P - N), so v and lambda are the speed and width of a WELL-FED front (nutrient 1); where the nutrient is depleted the front is slower and the derivation is a parametrisation, not the model's front. Accepted on 2026-10-01.
_twospecies: The four two-compartment parameters, fitted for the first time here (the class config carries placeholders, no sensitivity analysis exists for them; every range is a design choice, no literature value is claimed). necrosis_rate (1/day, log-uniform 0.01-1.0): the rate at which proliferative cells turn necrotic where the nutrient is below nutrient_threshold (a smooth switch of steepness 50 in the solver); the range spans necrosis time scales of 1 to 100 days, from a core that dies within days of starving to one that barely converts within the horizon. nutrient_threshold (nutrient level, linear 0.1-0.9): the nutrient field starts at 1 inside tissue and is only consumed, so the switch level is a fraction of the initial supply; the band leaves out the ends where the switch never (below 0.1) or always (above 0.9) fires in a consumed region. nutrient_diffusivity (mm^2/day, log-uniform 0.01-1.0) and nutrient_consumption_rate (1/day per unit P, log-uniform 0.01-1.0): together they set the depletion length sqrt(nutrient_diffusivity / nutrient_consumption_rate) of the nutrient around a dense tumour, here 0.1 to 10 mm, which is the scale on which a necrotic core forms inside a tumour of a few centimetres. The cap of nutrient_diffusivity is the time step's: the solver's stability rule for the two-compartment model is n_steps >= stopping_time * max(white_matter_diffusivity, nutrient_diffusivity) / h^2 * nt_multiplier (8) + 300 with h = 1 mm, and the fit fixes n_steps at 12 steps per day, so a nutrient diffusivity above about 1.3 mm^2/day would force the design-time check to raise the step count for every evaluation; 1.0 mm^2/day is also the cap of the tumour diffusivity (0.25 mm/day x 8 mm / 2). The consumption cap 1.0 /day keeps the explicit reaction step stable at dt = 1/12 day. The nutrient is not scored: the objective compares P + N with the pre-op necrotic + enhancing core and P alone with the post-op enhancing tumour (the scripts' core rule since 2026-10-01); the whole-tumour Dice is recorded from P + N but is not part of the default objective.
_starts: Sweep starts come from the isotropic sub-01 sweep (no two-compartment sweep exists): the shared factors are converted from the sweep rows, the four two-compartment factors take the script's SWEEP_FILL_VALUES (necrosis_rate 0.02, nutrient_threshold 0.15, nutrient_diffusivity 0.5, nutrient_consumption_rate 0.02: a well-fed tumour with a depletion length of 5 mm and a necrosis time scale of 50 days, a little inside the range ends so that the first proposals are not clipped; recorded as filled in starts.json), and the proxy ranking uses the sweep's isotropic Dice. The midpoint of the four ranges is NOT a usable start: with a depletion length of 1 mm and the switch at 0.5 the viable cells turn necrotic throughout and P reaches the core threshold nowhere after the surgery (fit_sub01_twospecies_2026-10-01_starved_start, every post-op core Dice of its first generation 0).
_units: front_speed_mm_per_day mm/day; front_width_mm mm; the derived white_matter_diffusivity mm^2/day and rho 1/day; seed_sigma_mm mm (the standard deviation of the seed profile); the derived gaussian_seed_diffusion_time mm^2 and gaussian_seed_mass density times mm^3; growth_length_mm mm; the derived preop_time days from the seed to the pre-op scan; seed_bbox_x/y/z dimensionless coordinates on the seedable voxels' bounding box; rt_alpha 1/Gy; chemo_kill_rate 1/day per mg/m^2; seed_peak_density a cell density (fraction of the carrying capacity); diffusivity_ratio dimensionless; rt_alpha_beta_ratio Gy; chemo_decay_rate 1/day. necrosis_rate 1/day; nutrient_threshold a nutrient level (fraction of the initial supply); nutrient_diffusivity mm^2/day; nutrient_consumption_rate 1/day per unit proliferative density.
